refusal.can_it_be_re_read: not from disk. The probe objects were built inside the trickle container's /work and no trickle volume survives (`podman volume ls` lists no trickle volume), so re-reading DW_AT_type means recompiling, which is a new compile run and not this task's scope.
refusal.what_is_on_disk: a DWARF parameter table per accepted probe, at the ANCHOR build, whose every row carries exactly two fields: `name` and `location`. `location` is the parameter's frame address (DW_OP_fbreg), not its width, and carries no encoding.
refusal.what_was_asked: per language, per scalar-core spelling, the DWARF byte size and encoding as the compiler recorded it, read from the parameter tables of the probes that used that spelling
refusal.who_narrowed_it: the reader shared by every probe lane, Research/op_pipeline/fold.py :: dwarf_rows, line 80: '`a=fbreg -4;b=fbreg -8` -> [{name, location}]'. The lane that produced the text it parses collects DW_AT_name and DW_AT_location off each DW_TAG_formal_parameter and never follows DW_AT_type.
refusal.why_the_join_cannot_be_made: brief §3 stop rule: the DWARF encoding decides the class and the width. With no DW_AT_byte_size and no DW_AT_encoding stored, a width would have to be assigned by hand from the spelling, which that rule forbids. Signedness in particular is not recoverable from the machine text: the register file separates integer from float, and the instruction suffix gives an access width, but nothing in the emitted text distinguishes a signed holder from an unsigned one.
